quiz.0.question: What is the difference between Montepulciano d'Abruzzo and Vino Nobile di Montepulciano?
quiz.0.options.0: The same wine under different names
quiz.0.options.1: Both the grape and the region differ
quiz.0.explanation: Montepulciano d'Abruzzo is made from the Montepulciano grape in Abruzzo; Vino Nobile di Montepulciano is made from Sangiovese in Tuscany.
quiz.1.question: What is the top quality level for Montepulciano d'Abruzzo?
quiz.1.explanation: Montepulciano d'Abruzzo Colline Teramane was promoted to DOCG in 2003: min. 90% Montepulciano, min. 1 year’s ageing, Riserva 3 years. Abruzzo’s other DOCG is Terre Tollesi / Tullum (2019).
quiz.2.question: What characterises Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo?
quiz.2.explanation: Cerasuolo comes from the dialect word cerasa (cherry). Made from min. 85% Montepulciano, it is deeper in colour than most rosés and complex, savoury and structured. It is a still rosé, not a sparkling wine.
quiz.3.question: What is the relationship between Trebbiano Abruzzese and Trebbiano Toscano?
quiz.3.options.1: Different varieties, but often confused and often co-planted
quiz.3.options.3: Trebbiano Toscano cannot be used in Trebbiano d'Abruzzo
quiz.3.explanation: Trebbiano Abruzzese and Trebbiano Toscano are different varieties but are often confused and often co-planted with Bombino Bianco; Trebbiano d'Abruzzo DOC allows all three (min. 85% combined). Trebbiano Abruzzese was once thought to be Bombino Bianco, but it is not.

slides.0.subtitle: Home of Montepulciano d'Abruzzo
slides.1.title: 🏔️ Between the Mountains and the Sea
slides.1.content:
Abruzzo lies in central Italy, with the Central Apennines (the Gran Sasso and Monti della Laga) to the west and the Adriatic Sea to the east. It is known for Montepulciano d'Abruzzo reds, Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo rosato and Trebbiano d'Abruzzo whites.

Abruzzo is the most mountainous region of central and southern Italy and one of its most densely planted wine regions; vineyards are concentrated in the coastal and middle hill bands, and about three-quarters of DOC/DOCG production is bottled as Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC.

slides.3.title: 🍇 Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC
slides.3.content:
🍷 Italy’s value champion

⚠️ Name check: Montepulciano d'Abruzzo (Montepulciano the grape + Abruzzo) ≠ Vino Nobile di Montepulciano (Sangiovese + a Tuscan town) — two completely different wines!

🍇 Grape and style

Grape: min. 85% Montepulciano

Style: from simple, fruity and easy-drinking to deep-coloured, concentrated, structured and oak-aged

Flavours: black cherry, plum, violet, spice, herbs

Riserva: min. 2 years’ ageing (at least 9 months in wood)

Scope: a regional DOC created in 1968 (Abruzzo’s first DOC), with 5 sub-zones

🏆 Quality levels

Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC: the base level

Colline Teramane DOCG:

  • The hills around Teramo, from the coast to the foothills of the Gran Sasso
  • Promoted to DOCG in 2003
  • Min. 90% Montepulciano (max. 10% Sangiovese)
  • Min. 1 year’s ageing; Riserva 3 years (1 year in wood)

🍽️ Pairing

  • 🐑 Arrosticini lamb skewers
  • 🍝 Chitarra pasta with meat sauce
  • 🥩 Grilled red meat, game
  • 🧀 Aged Pecorino
  • 🍄 Wild-mushroom risotto
slides.4.title: 🍷 The Montepulciano Grape
slides.4.content:
🍇 Montepulciano: late-ripening, vigorous, deep-coloured and tannic

Key characteristics

  • Native: native to Abruzzo and its most widely planted grape; most Montepulciano is planted in Abruzzo
  • Late-ripening: needs a long, warm growing season to ripen fully
  • Vigorous, thick-skinned: pronounced tannins and high anthocyanin content
  • Bulk wine: formerly widely used as vino da taglio (bulk blending wine)

Relationship with Sangiovese

  • Historical confusion: Montepulciano was long confused with Sangiovese
  • Not closely related: the two are not close relatives
  • Name trap: Montepulciano is not native to the Tuscan town of Montepulciano; Vino Nobile di Montepulciano is made from Sangiovese
  • Partner: Colline Teramane DOCG may include up to 10% Sangiovese

🍷 Styles by quality level

Basic DOC

Easy everyday drinking, fruit-led

Black cherry, plum, soft tannins

Drink: now–5 years, €8–18

Colline Teramane DOCG

More structured, more concentrated

Black fruit, leather, spice

Drink: 5–15 years, €20–50

DOCG Riserva

Top quality, oak-aged

Complex, smoky, dried fruit, minerality

Drink: 8–20 years, €35–80

Value tip: a basic Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC at €8–15 usually delivers generous fruit and a smooth palate — an excellent introduction to Italian red wine.
slides.5.title: ⚪ Trebbiano d'Abruzzo DOC: The White Fights Back
slides.5.content:
💡 Key point: Trebbiano d'Abruzzo DOC is historically Abruzzo’s flagship white and may use three varieties: Trebbiano Abruzzese, Trebbiano Toscano and Bombino Bianco. Trebbiano Abruzzese was once thought to be the same as Bombino Bianco and is often confused with Trebbiano Toscano, but the three are different varieties — and are often co-planted in the same vineyard. Valentini and Emidio Pepe have proved its remarkable ageing potential.

📜 DOC rules

IWS key points

Grapes: min. 85% Trebbiano Abruzzese and/or Trebbiano Toscano and/or Bombino Bianco

Superiore: higher minimum alcohol

Riserva: min. 18 months’ ageing

Trebbiano Toscano: Abruzzo’s most widely planted white grape, often blended with Trebbiano Abruzzese

Trebbiano Abruzzese: uncertain origin; traditional (possibly native) to Abruzzo

✅ Quality style

The quality route

Past: mass-produced, neutral wines that dragged its reputation down

Today: low yields, fully ripe fruit, made in large casks (botti) or stainless steel

Flavours: white peach, apricot, almond, minerality

Ageing: top wines can age for decades

Benchmarks: Valentini, Emidio Pepe
slides.6.title: 🌸 Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo DOC
slides.6.content:
🌸 Cerasuolo (meaning “cherry-coloured”) comes from the dialect word “cerasa” (cherry). It is Abruzzo’s regional rosato and became a DOC in its own right in 2010. Min. 85% Montepulciano, with a Superiore category (higher minimum alcohol). Compared with other rosés it is deeper in colour with more intense cherry, and complex, savoury and structured.

🍷 Winemaking

Maceration: a short maceration extracts Montepulciano’s abundant anthocyanins

Colour: deep pink to light red (cherry red)

Fermentation: cool fermentation in stainless steel to keep the fruit

🌸 Flavour profile

Flavours: red cherry, strawberry, raspberry, violet, spice

Style: complex, savoury, structured

Note: Cerasuolo is a still rosé, not a sparkling wine

🍽️ Pairing

🍝 Pasta with tomato sauce

🍤 Grilled seafood, fried fish

🥗 Summer salads, cold cuts

🍕 Pizza, tomato dishes
slides.7.title: 🎯 How to Choose Quality Abruzzo Wine
slides.7.content:
🎯 Abruzzo wines range from €8 to €180 — a huge price spread. A few simple principles will help you find genuinely good wines on a sensible budget.

🍷 Four rules for reds

🏆 Choose Colline Teramane DOCG

The most consistent higher-tier appellation, worth ageing, with structure and depth

⭐ Look for Riserva

DOC Riserva is aged at least 2 years, DOCG Riserva 3 years — more complex and elegant

🏡 Choose small quality producers

Tighter yield control and higher quality; favour producers known for strict management

🌱 Traditional icons

Emidio Pepe, Valentini and Masciarelli are the benchmark producers listed by IWS

⚪ Choosing whites and rosés

❌ Avoid the cheapest versions

Trebbiano under €10 is usually mass-produced and ordinary

🌟 Renowned quality producers

Valentini (legendary), Emidio Pepe (organic), Tiberio (modern)

📋 Try native white grapes

Pecorino and Passerina have become very popular; Terre Tollesi (Tullum) DOCG whites are based on the two

🌸 Try Cerasuolo

A deep-coloured rosé with great value — the ideal food wine between white and red
slides.8.title: 🍽️ Abruzzo Food and Wine Pairing
slides.8.content:
🐑 Mountain cooking meets seafood

Abruzzo’s cuisine combines meat and cheese from the mountains with seafood from the coast — rustic in style, with excellent ingredients.

🐑 Arrosticini lamb skewers

  • Abruzzo’s most iconic dish
  • ✅ Montepulciano d'Abruzzo
  • ✅ Colline Teramane Riserva

🍝 Maccheroni alla Chitarra

  • Pasta cut on a guitar-like tool
  • ✅ Montepulciano (with meat sauce)
  • ✅ Trebbiano (with seafood sauce)

🦞 Brodetto di Pesce

  • Abruzzo-style Adriatic fish soup
  • ✅ Trebbiano d'Abruzzo
  • ✅ Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo

🧀 Pecorino Abruzzese

  • Abruzzo sheep’s-milk cheese
  • ✅ Aged Montepulciano (aged cheese)
  • ✅ Trebbiano (fresh cheese)
slides.9.title: 🏺 The History of Abruzzo Wine
slides.9.content:
⏳ From ancient Rome to a modern industry: Abruzzo’s wine history goes back to Roman times — Pliny the Elder mentioned the wines of the Teramo area (the land of the Praetutii), and the poet Ovid was born in Sulmo (today’s Sulmona). Abruzzo once had a rich ampelographic heritage, until phylloxera decimated its vineyards.

Ancient Rome

🏺 The Roman era

Pliny the Elder recorded the wines of the Praetutii (the Teramo area); Ovid was born in Sulmo (today’s Sulmona, home of the Terre dei Peligni sub-zone).

Middle Ages

⛪ The abbey of San Clemente a Casauria

Founded in 871 in the Aterno-Pescara valley; today’s Terre di Casauria sub-zone is named after it.

19th–20th c.

🐛 Phylloxera and the bulk-wine era

Phylloxera decimated the vineyards and much of the varietal heritage was lost; replanting focused on Montepulciano and Trebbiano, and large volumes were shipped north as vino da taglio (bulk blending wine).

DOC / DOCG

📜 1968–2003

In 1968 Montepulciano d'Abruzzo became Abruzzo’s first DOC; in 2003 Colline Teramane was promoted to DOCG.

New era

🌸 2010–2019

In 2010 Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo became a DOC in its own right; in 2019 Terre Tollesi (Tullum) was promoted to become Abruzzo’s second DOCG.

slides.10.title: 🍇 Abruzzo Grape Varieties in Full (IWS Course Material)
slides.10.content:
🍇 Three grapes dominate

Red grapes

  • Montepulciano: native to Abruzzo and its most planted grape, dominating most appellations
  • Sangiovese: a minor variety; Colline Teramane DOCG may include up to 10%
  • Most of the vineyard area is planted to red grapes; international varieties play only a minor role

White grapes

  • Trebbiano Toscano: the most planted white grape, often blended with Trebbiano Abruzzese
  • Trebbiano Abruzzese: uncertain origin, traditional to Abruzzo; once thought to be the same as Bombino Bianco
  • Others: Pecorino, Passerina, Cococciola, Montonico Bianco, Malvasia, Falanghina

🍷 Key grapes compared

Montepulciano

Late-ripening, vigorous, thick-skinned, pronounced tannins, high in anthocyanins

Styles range from simple, easy-drinking, high-acid and inexpensive to deep-coloured, concentrated, structured, high-alcohol, oak-aged and expensive; also widely used for rosato

The soul of Abruzzo

Trebbiano Abruzzese

Often confused with Trebbiano Toscano

Trebbiano Abruzzese, Trebbiano Toscano and Bombino Bianco are often co-planted

The core of Trebbiano d'Abruzzo

Pecorino

Considered native to southern Marche on the border with Abruzzo (not native to Abruzzo)

Naturally high in sugar and acid; popularity and plantings have increased recently, mostly as a varietal white

A white on the rise

IWS exam points: Montepulciano is not native to the Tuscan town of Montepulciano and is not closely related to Sangiovese; Pecorino is a white grape native to southern Marche.
slides.11.title: 🏆 Montepulciano d'Abruzzo: 5 Sub-zones and Two DOCGs
slides.11.content:
🏆 Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC is a regional DOC with 5 sub-zones, which require a higher share of the grape than the DOC (min. 85%). Colline Teramane was originally one of them before becoming a separate DOCG in 2003.

⛪ Casauria / Terre di Casauria

Location: south-west of Chieti along the Aterno-Pescara river

Requires 100% Montepulciano

Name: from the abbey of San Clemente a Casauria

🏔️ Terre dei Vestini

Location: from Pescara up to the foothills of the Gran Sasso

Min. 90% Montepulciano

Key facts: the hills of Pescara province

⛰️ Alto Tirino

Location: a high-altitude sub-zone in the south-eastern foothills of the Gran Sasso

Min. 95% Montepulciano

Key facts: inland uplands of L'Aquila province

🏞️ Terre dei Peligni

Location: the Peligna valley around the town of Sulmona, at high altitude

Min. 95% Montepulciano

Key facts: the birthplace of the poet Ovid

🌊 Teate

Location: from Pescara and Chieti to the Molise border

Min. 90% Montepulciano

Name: Teate is the ancient name of Chieti

🏆 Montepulciano d'Abruzzo Colline Teramane DOCG (2003)

Location: the hills around Teramo, from the Adriatic coast to the foothills of the Gran Sasso and Monti della Laga

Rules: min. 90% Montepulciano (max. 10% Sangiovese); min. 1 year’s ageing, Riserva 3 years (1 year in wood)

⭐ Terre Tollesi / Tullum DOCG (2019)

Location: around the town of Tollo in Chieti province, near the coast (Tullum is the Latin name of Tollo)

Rules: whites based on Passerina and Pecorino, reds based on Montepulciano; still and spumante (sparkling) styles
slides.12.title: 🌿 Topography, Soils and the Pergola Abruzzese (IWS Course Material)
slides.12.content:
⛰️ The interplay of sea and mountains: Mediterranean near the coast, continental inland. Abruzzo is mostly mountains (the Central Apennines, Gran Sasso and Monti della Laga); vineyards are concentrated in the coastal and middle hill bands, and there are no large coastal plains.

🌊 The coastal hill band

  • Soils: clay of marine origin
  • Climate: Mediterranean, moderated by the Adriatic
  • Rivers: the Tronto, Vomano, Tordino, Aterno-Pescara and Sangro flow from the mountains to the sea
  • Centre of gravity: Chieti is by far the largest province (over 80% of the region’s vineyards according to the Consorzio), followed by Pescara and Teramo; L'Aquila has less than 1%

⛰️ The middle hill band and mountain basins

  • Soils: marl, sandstone, clay — varied, but mostly containing clay
  • Climate: increasingly continental inland, with wide diurnal ranges
  • Mountain basins: Valle Peligna, Conca Aquilana, Conca del Fucino
  • Sub-zones: Alto Tirino and Terre dei Peligni lie in the high inland areas

🌿 Abruzzo’s training systems

🌿
Pergola Abruzzese

The traditional overhead trellis, still the most widespread training system

→
📈
High yields

The pergola gives high yields, and much of the crop once became vino da taglio bulk blending wine

→
✂️
Cordone Speronato

New vineyards are mostly planted in rows and trained to spur-pruned cordon

→
🏆
Quality focus

Yield control and selection have taken Abruzzo from bulk wine to fine wine
slides.13.title: 🍷 The Trebbiano Revival and the Art of Cerasuolo
slides.13.content:
🔬 The truth about Trebbiano

Three varieties, one DOC

  • Trebbiano Abruzzese: uncertain origin, traditional (possibly native) to Abruzzo
  • And Bombino Bianco: once thought to be the same variety, but it is not
  • And Trebbiano Toscano: often confused; Trebbiano Toscano is Abruzzo’s most planted white grape
  • Co-planting: the three are often planted together, and the rules allow all three in Trebbiano d'Abruzzo

The Valentini legend

  • A traditional estate in Loreto Aprutino, Pescara province
  • Only the best grapes are bottled; the rest is sold
  • Made and aged in large casks (botti)
  • Its Trebbiano d'Abruzzo is famed for remarkable longevity

🌸 How Cerasuolo is made

🍇
Harvest

Ripe Montepulciano is picked (min. 85%)

→
🕐
Short maceration

Montepulciano is so rich in anthocyanins that a short maceration gives a deep cherry colour

→
🧃
Run-off and pressing

Deeper than most rosés; the name comes from the dialect word cerasa (cherry)

→
🌸
Fermentation

Intense cherry; complex, savoury and structured; Superiore has a higher minimum alcohol
slides.14.title: 🏆 Abruzzo’s Legendary Estates
slides.14.content:
🍷 The drivers of Abruzzo’s quality revolution: from the traditionalists Emidio Pepe and Valentini to the modernist Masciarelli, these estates have shown over decades that Abruzzo is more than a source of cheap wine.

EP

est. 1964

Emidio Pepe 🌿

Standing: Abruzzo’s natural-wine legend — hand-harvested, foot-crushed, wild yeasts, unfiltered

Location: Torano Nuovo, Teramo province; organic and biodynamic farming

Philosophy: minimal intervention, with old vintages kept at the estate for a long time and released late

• Montepulciano d'Abruzzo: €60–90 (very long ageing potential)

• Trebbiano d'Abruzzo: €50–75 (exceptionally complex)

• Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo: €40–55

Note: old vintages are decanted and rebottled before shipping

VT

est. 1650s

Valentini 👑

Standing: one of Italy’s most mysterious legendary estates, uncompromising perfectionists

Location: Loreto Aprutino, Pescara province

Philosophy: only the best grapes are bottled under the estate name and the rest is sold; in poor vintages nothing may be bottled at all

• Trebbiano d'Abruzzo: €100–180 (remarkable longevity; one of Italy’s most revered whites)

• Montepulciano d'Abruzzo: €80–130

• Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo: €60–90

Warning: extremely scarce — pre-order through a trusted importer

Masciarelli 🏆

📍 San Martino sulla Marrucina, Chieti province; a modernist standard-bearer

Flagship: Villa Gemma

Montepulciano DOC: €12–20

Villa Gemma Riserva: €50–80

Ageing: 5–15 years

Cataldi Madonna 🌱

📍 Ofena, L'Aquila province; the Alto Tirino sub-zone area

An inland mountain estate; a leading Cerasuolo producer

Montepulciano DOC: €15–25

Cerasuolo Superiore: €20–30

Ageing: 3–10 years

Tiberio 🔬

📍 Cugnoli, Pescara province; founded 2000

Modern, refined style; known for Trebbiano Abruzzese and Pecorino

Montepulciano DOC: €16–25

Trebbiano d'Abruzzo: €20–30

Ageing: 3–8 years

Illuminati 🌟

📍 Controguerra, Teramo province

Balancing tradition and modernity; a Colline Teramane standard-bearer

Colline Teramane DOCG: €20–35

Pieluni Riserva: €35–55

Ageing: 5–20 years

💰 Price tiers and buying tips

💚 Entry level

Drink: now–5 years; a great choice for beginners

slides.17.points.1: ✓ Montepulciano is native to Abruzzo and its most planted grape: late-ripening, thick-skinned, with pronounced tannins; it is not native to the Tuscan town of Montepulciano, nor closely related to Sangiovese
slides.17.points.2: ✓ Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC (1968) was Abruzzo’s first DOC: min. 85% Montepulciano, Riserva 2 years (9 months in wood), 5 sub-zones, about three-quarters of DOC/G production

slides.17.points.4: ✓ Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo (cerasa = cherry) is the regional rosato: min. 85% Montepulciano, deep in colour, savoury and structured
slides.17.points.5: ✓ Trebbiano d'Abruzzo: min. 85% Trebbiano Abruzzese and/or Trebbiano Toscano and/or Bombino Bianco; Riserva 18 months

slides.17.points.7: ✓ Key producers: Emidio Pepe, Valentini, Masciarelli

slides.18.questions.1.explanation: Montepulciano d'Abruzzo Colline Teramane was promoted to DOCG in 2003: min. 90% Montepulciano, min. 1 year’s ageing, Riserva 3 years. Abruzzo’s other DOCG is Terre Tollesi / Tullum (2019).

slides.18.questions.7.options.1: B. False: it is considered native to southern Marche, on the border with Abruzzo
slides.18.questions.7.options.2: C. False: it is a red grape

slides.18.questions.8.question: What was Abruzzo’s first DOC?
slides.18.questions.8.explanation: Montepulciano d'Abruzzo became Abruzzo’s first DOC in 1968 and is also the largest appellation by volume, accounting for about three-quarters of DOC/G production.
slides.18.questions.9.question: Which Montepulciano d'Abruzzo sub-zone requires 100% Montepulciano?
slides.18.questions.9.explanation: Casauria (Terre di Casauria), south-west of Chieti along the Aterno-Pescara river, requires 100% Montepulciano; Alto Tirino and Terre dei Peligni require min. 95%, Terre dei Vestini and Teate min. 90%.
